findings.issue_text: In UsernamePasswordForm, conditional passkey setup logic is inverted: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null, so fillContextForm() is never invoked on fresh login pages, and conditional passkey UI only appears after a failed attempt

UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field) silently skips re-enabling conditional UI when the username was unknown (e.g. after a typo'd username), so the user can no longer switch to passkey login on that page
Tests only assert the webauthn form after a failed attempt, so the conditional passkey regression on initial page render is not covered

WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse gates on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note which is absent during first-factor conditional passkey failures, and once set to true the note persists for the rest of the login attempt, causing subsequent non-re-auth form renderings to incorrectly get USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED (e.g. identity-first or recovery forms)

UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only definition added in this PR is the one-arg version in UsernamePasswordForm, which UsernameForm neither extends nor can reach — possibly a compile error or an unverifiable divergent definition

WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm now gates the identified-user branch on the overridable shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context) hook, which returns false unconditionally in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator — even during 2FA/re-auth when the user is identified, so authenticator listing and the no-credentials challenge branch are now unreachable for that subclass
Fragile test idiom in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey: try/assertThat/fail wrapped in catch(Exception) only works because findElement throws before the assertion when the element is absent
Removal of events.clear() in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey leaves stale events in the stream before the final expectLogin(), weakening the assertions

In UsernamePasswordForm.java (~line 110–160, authenticate() and challenge() overloads), the new guard isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null before calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context), so on a normal first-factor login (where context.getUser() is null when the username/password page renders) the WebAuthn conditional-UI form data (ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, challenge attributes) is never populated — a functional regression breaking passkey autofill on the primary login page (P2).

In UsernameForm.java (~line 47), the condition 'if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())' is based only on the realm-level passkeys policy rather than whether the re-authenticating user actually possesses a passkey credential, forcing users with only a password (no WebAuthn credential or linked IdP) back to username/password interaction during prompt=login re-authentication instead of the previous seamless context.success() — a behavioral regression affecting all users in passkey-enabled realms and potentially breaking custom flows relying on the auto-skip (P3).

Possible duplicate fillContextForm / credential load: webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) runs in authenticate(...) and may be invoked again via challenge(context, formData) delegating to challenge(context, error, field), causing WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean (which loads all user WebAuthn credentials) to be built twice per login page render (UsernamePasswordForm.java ~line 113/136)

On the re-auth error path (badPasswordHandler → challenge), fillContextForm now runs on every failed password attempt, adding a per-attempt credential store query plus policy lookup that previously did not occur for already-identified users

fillContextForm now fires in widened conditions — for identified users on the username/password page in conditional-passkeys realms and on error re-renders via the new challenge(..., error, field) hook — each call streaming and materializing all of the user's WebAuthn credentials, adding a credential-store round trip to common flows where it previously didn't occur

Conditional passkey UI (discoverable/passkey autofill) is no longer offered when the user is unidentified on the UsernamePasswordForm login page: the new gate requires user != null, but conditional passkeys are by definition a first-step credential for unidentified users, breaking discoverable-passkey login on realms using the combined username+password form. The PR's own test webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication expects the webauthn form at initial login where context.getUser() is null, which this gate makes impossible.

Re-authentication page shape drift: UsernameForm.java:47 now shows the username form during re-auth whenever conditional passkeys are enabled, even for broker-less users who previously skipped it, adding an extra interactive step; additionally UsernameForm's error paths do not call AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError, so a failed username form during re-auth in a passkeys realm renders as a regular login form with registration link visible and editable username, leaking inconsistent re-auth page shape.

USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH constant in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58 changed from protected static final to public static final and now consumed cross-package via static import in AuthenticUtils, widening an internal auth-session note key into public API with no documentation of when it is set/cleared, risking conflicts with third-party authenticators defining identically-named note semantics.

Conditional passkey UI data no longer populated when user is unknown (initial login or failed username): new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) gate requires user != null, inverting the old condition, so fillContextForm is never invoked when context.getUser() == null, causing the passkey affordance to vanish mid-flow in UsernamePasswordForm

Users whose only credential is a broker/IDP link are now forced through the password form during re-authentication: the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() short-circuit in UsernameForm fires before hasLinkedBrokers is consulted, skipping the immediate context.success() fast path for broker-linked users

shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator returns false unconditionally, so on error pages with an identified user the concrete authenticator list can never render, falling back to the unidentified-user path with the username hidden and no actionable credential selection

setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError behavior (username hidden on failed re-auth) is never verified: no test asserts the username input is hidden or registration link removed after a failed-password step in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, only the 'Invalid password.' error message is checked

WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse change is completely untested: no test triggers a failing/invalid passkey during re-authentication and asserts the resulting form state for the new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in the passkey error path

Passkey re-auth tests (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication in PasskeysUsernameFormTest and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) cannot distinguish re-authentication from plain SSO: no assertion of the re-auth interstitial message, so if prompt=login were ignored the tests would still pass

Missing test for UsernameForm with conditional passkeys and a user who has no passkey credentials: the new !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() condition may incorrectly show an editable username form during re-auth for users without WebAuthn credentials

Dead/contradictory assertion pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey: assertThat(..., nullValue()) is unreachable dead code since driver.findElement throws NoSuchElementException; should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)

Failed-login error events are silently discarded in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey: events.clear() is called without asserting the expected LOGIN_ERROR event (Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS, user set)
No test covers re-authentication with a non-discoverable key: all new re-auth tests use discoverable/external resident keys despite the conditional-UI re-auth changes

Duplication of the 'user already set' auth-note check logic: `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` in AuthenticatorUtils.java:126-129 re-implements the existing `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` predicate instead of delegating to it, creating two independent implementations that can drift

Cross-package leak of internal constant: `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` was widened from `protected` to `public` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58 / AuthenticatorUtils.java:35) solely for a static import, promoting an internal stringly-typed protocol into public API surface

`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` defined in both UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162 and UsernameForm.java:47 with different signatures and divergent semantics (one requires `user != null`), a drift trap; also the user-null check is a semantic mismatch in a realm-policy 'enabled' check

Dead code: `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64-66` unconditionally returns `false` from `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`, making the authenticator-listing branch in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` (lines 100-119) unreachable and making `isUserIdentified` dependent on an overridable hook

Three near-verbatim copies of the same re-authentication test across PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:269-318, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:260-315, and PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest; shared helpers should be extracted for the login/re-auth/event-assert sequences

Fragile 'assert element absent' idiom in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest that swallows arbitrary exceptions via `catch (Exception e)`; should use `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` as done in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, and the inconsistency between idioms adds confusion

Comment/naming drift in WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:97-101: the `user` local is fetched but the branch condition no longer references it, and the old '2 Factor Scenario' comment no longer matches the code delegated to a hook

Broker-linked users lose the re-auth fast-path when conditional passkeys are enabled: the hasLinkedBrokers branch in UsernameForm.java:47 is unreachable because the && short-circuits on !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(), forcing all re-authenticating users through the username form with no check for existing passkey credentials

User-switch during re-authentication is now possible via the username form: submitted username flows into the normal setUser/user-lookup path without validation that it matches the expected re-auth user, allowing identity switching in step-up flows

Passkey form data is no longer filled when no user is set due to inverted condition on the error path (UsernamePasswordForm.java:113/137): error re-renders after failed first-attempt silently drop the passkey UI because fillContextForm is never invoked

shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators change in WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100 makes fillContextForm semantics override-dependent, risking inconsistent behavior with isUserIdentified handling in future subclasses (maintenance hazard)

Weak assertion pattern in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest: try/catch-fail idiom around driver.findElement can pass for the wrong reason (element present but findElement throwing for timing reasons is swallowed as expected)

Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)`, the diff changes the condition for calling `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` from `context.getUser() == null && ...isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, where `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. This means when the username is unknown/not resolved (e.g., typo -> `context.getUser()` stays null), the WebAuthn/passkeys context is no longer populated during the error challenge, so the page can lose the passkey UI/ability to switch to passkey login after such an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests only assert the webauthn form after a failed attempt, so the conditional passkey regression on initial page render is not covered

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/updates multiple tests that assert the presence/absence of the WebAuthn form on the initial render of the relevant login/reauth pages, not only after a failed attempt. Examples: PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest now asserts `driver.findElement(...//form[@id='webauth']...)` is not null immediately after the username/password page is presented (before submitting an invalid password). PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest asserts the webauthn form is present right after opening re-authentication with `prompt=login` (before entering a wrong password), and also has tests asserting it is absent on initial render when passkeys are disabled (`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`). Therefore the claim that initial page render regressions aren’t covered is contradicted by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse gates on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note which is absent during first-factor conditional passkey failures, and once set to true the note persists for the rest of the login attempt, causing subsequent non-re-auth form renderings to incorrectly get USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED (e.g. identity-first or recovery forms)

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse simply calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context), which only *reads* the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note and, if it parses to true, sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on the current LoginFormsProvider. If the note is absent (null), Boolean.parseBoolean returns false and nothing happens—so there is no shown defect for first-factor failures. The diff also does not show this helper being invoked from “identity-first or recovery forms”, so the claimed cross-form incorrect hiding/disabling is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` from `if (user != null)` to `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context))`, and introduces an overridable hook that defaults to `context.getUser() != null`. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` then overrides this hook to always return `false`, which makes the entire identified-user branch (including creation of `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` and the empty-authenticators handling inside that block) unreachable for that subclass, even when `context.getUser()` is set (e.g., re-auth). This is a real behavioral change; whether it is a defect is not provable from the diff alone, but it is a specific, diff-grounded concern about potentially skipping important handling for identified users.

adjudication.rationale: In `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, although an earlier `events.clear()` after `logout()` was removed, the test later calls `events.clear()` immediately before each `events.expectLogin()` (once before the passkey re-authentication assertion, and again before the final password re-authentication assertion). Therefore no stale events remain in the stream before the final `expectLogin()`, and the assertions are not weakened in the way described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In UsernamePasswordForm.java (~line 110–160, authenticate() and challenge() overloads), the new guard isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) requires user != null before calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context), so on a normal first-factor login (where context.getUser() is null when the username/password page renders) the WebAuthn conditional-UI form data (ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, challenge attributes) is never populated — a functional regression breaking passkey autofill on the primary login page (P2).

adjudication.rationale: In UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() the call to webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) was moved out and is now guarded by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which returns true only when user != null. Previously, authenticate() populated WebAuthn/passkeys form context whenever passkeys were enabled (and challenge(error, field) explicitly did so when context.getUser() == null). The new guards in both authenticate() and challenge(error, field) therefore skip fillContextForm on the initial username/password screen when context.getUser() is null, so the conditional-UI attributes would not be set in that common path, matching the reported regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In UsernameForm.java (~line 47), the condition 'if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())' is based only on the realm-level passkeys policy rather than whether the re-authenticating user actually possesses a passkey credential, forcing users with only a password (no WebAuthn credential or linked IdP) back to username/password interaction during prompt=login re-authentication instead of the previous seamless context.success() — a behavioral regression affecting all users in passkey-enabled realms and potentially breaking custom flows relying on the auto-skip (P3).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernameForm.authenticate() from skipping the form whenever `context.getUser() != null` (and no linked brokers) to skipping only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`. The new gating is unrelated to whether the already-identified (re-authenticating) user actually has any WebAuthn/passkey credential; elsewhere in this diff the analogous enablement check in `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` is based on `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` (realm/feature-level) plus `user != null`, not user credential presence. Therefore, in passkeys-enabled realms, password-only users who previously hit `context.success()` during re-auth will now be forced through the username step (and likely subsequent password step), which is a behavioral regression introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Possible duplicate fillContextForm / credential load: webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) runs in authenticate(...) and may be invoked again via challenge(context, formData) delegating to challenge(context, error, field), causing WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean (which loads all user WebAuthn credentials) to be built twice per login page render (UsernamePasswordForm.java ~line 113/136)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate(...)` calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only before invoking `challenge(context, formData)` (the MultivaluedMap overload). The only other added `fillContextForm` call is in the separate override `challenge(context, String error, String field)`, which is used for error challenges and is not shown to be invoked from `challenge(context, formData)` in this diff. Additionally, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(...)` to return `false`, so `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm(...)` will *not* build `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` (the expensive credential load) during passkeys conditional UI flows. Thus the claim that WebAuthn credentials are loaded twice per page render is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: On the re-auth error path (badPasswordHandler → challenge), fillContextForm now runs on every failed password attempt, adding a per-attempt credential store query plus policy lookup that previously did not occur for already-identified users

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, String, String) from only calling webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when context.getUser() == null to calling it when isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) (which requires user != null). On the badPasswordHandler error path, the user is typically already set during re-authentication, so the error challenge will now invoke fillContextForm on each failed password attempt, whereas previously it would not. Since WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm builds a WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean for the user (likely involving credential lookups), this is a real per-attempt overhead change, but it’s a performance/behavioral concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: fillContextForm now fires in widened conditions — for identified users on the username/password page in conditional-passkeys realms and on error re-renders via the new challenge(..., error, field) hook — each call streaming and materializing all of the user's WebAuthn credentials, adding a credential-store round trip to common flows where it previously didn't occur

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `UsernamePasswordForm` now calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() != null` and passkeys are enabled (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)`), both during initial `authenticate()` and during error challenges (`challenge(context, error, field)`). Previously, the error-path hook only filled context when `context.getUser() == null`, so identified-user/reauth flows would not trigger this. Since `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` constructs `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` for the user (which plausibly consults credential storage), this is a concrete, diff-grounded potential performance/extra-IO concern in more common re-authentication flows, but not a verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavioral change in `UsernameForm.authenticate`: it used to short-circuit re-authentication whenever `context.getUser() != null` (and no linked brokers), but now it only short-circuits when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`. That can introduce an extra username-form step during re-auth when conditional passkeys are enabled, even for broker-less users. However, the claim about `UsernameForm` error paths not calling `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` is not verifiable from this diff: the added helper is clearly used in password/passkey error handling (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler`, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`), and no `UsernameForm` error-path changes are shown here.

The diff does not show documentation or lifecycle (set/clear) changes for the note, so the “no documentation of when it is set/cleared” part is not addressed here, but the key visibility/API widening itself is verifiable and non-trivial. It’s not a direct correctness defect proven by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the new guard `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { if (!this.hasLinkedBrokers(context)) context.success(); }` only changes behavior for users who would have taken the fast-path `context.success()` (i.e., those with `context.getUser() != null` AND `hasLinkedBrokers(context) == false`). Broker/IDP-linked users have `hasLinkedBrokers(context) == true`, so they were already excluded from the fast-path before this diff, and the finding’s claim that broker/IDP-only users are newly forced through a password form is not supported by the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators override in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator returns false unconditionally, so on error pages with an identified user the concrete authenticator list can never render, falling back to the unidentified-user path with the username hidden and no actionable credential selection

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` to consult `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` explicitly overrides it to return `false` with the comment “Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys”. From the diff alone, this does not demonstrate broken behavior: it only suppresses the per-user authenticator *list* for the conditional-UI authenticator, and the tests added/updated expect the WebAuthn form (`//form[@id='webauth']`) to still be present during re-authentication/error flows. The claim that it “falls back … with … no actionable credential selection” is not verifiable from the shown code and appears contrary to the intended change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError behavior (username hidden on failed re-auth) is never verified: no test asserts the username input is hidden or registration link removed after a failed-password step in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, only the 'Invalid password.' error message is checked

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/relocates re-authentication error UI setup into `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)`, which sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` when `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` is true (new static import + constant made `public`). The new test `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` exercises a failed-password during re-authentication and only asserts the error text (`"Invalid password."`) and that the WebAuthn form is still present; it does not assert that the username field is hidden or registration is disabled after the failed step. So the finding about missing verification of this newly centralized behavior is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse change is completely untested: no test triggers a failing/invalid passkey during re-authentication and asserts the resulting form state for the new setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call in the passkey error path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` by calling `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (new re-authentication form-state setup on the passkey error path). The added/modified tests exercise successful passkey re-authentication and some password-failure scenarios, but none in the diff appear to intentionally trigger a *passkey failure* during re-authentication and then assert the resulting form state (e.g., username hidden/registration disabled) that this new call is meant to enforce. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Passkey re-auth tests (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication in PasskeysUsernameFormTest and PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest) cannot distinguish re-authentication from plain SSO: no assertion of the re-auth interstitial message, so if prompt=login were ignored the tests would still pass

adjudication.rationale: In both newly added tests `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` (in `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`), the re-auth step uses `oauth.loginForm().prompt(OIDCLoginProtocol.PROMPT_VALUE_LOGIN).open();` and then immediately asserts `appPage.assertCurrent()` and expects a `LOGIN` event, without asserting any re-authentication UI/interstitial (e.g., login page with an info message like "Please re-authenticate to continue"). As written, if `prompt=login` were ignored or satisfied via plain SSO (auto-login) and still produced a login event, these tests could still pass without proving the re-auth flow actually occurred.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test for UsernameForm with conditional passkeys and a user who has no passkey credentials: the new !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() condition may incorrectly show an editable username form during re-auth for users without WebAuthn credentials

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new branching in `UsernameForm.authenticate`: it now skips the username form during re-authentication only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (previously it skipped whenever `context.getUser() != null`). This is nontrivial new behavior, but the added tests around re-authentication primarily target `UsernamePasswordForm`/WebAuthn flows and do not cover the specific `UsernameForm` case of re-authentication with conditional passkeys enabled when the identified user lacks WebAuthn/passkey credentials. The finding is about missing targeted coverage for this new conditional path rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/contradictory assertion pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey: assertThat(..., nullValue()) is unreachable dead code since driver.findElement throws NoSuchElementException; should use Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)

adjudication.rationale: In `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the test uses `driver.findElement(...)` inside a `try` and then `assertThat(..., nullValue())` followed by `fail(...)`. `findElement` either returns a non-null `WebElement` or throws `NoSuchElementException`, so the `nullValue()` assertion is redundant/contradictory (it can only ever fail if reached). The `fail(...)` line is effectively unreachable because either `findElement` throws before it or the assertion fails before it. This is a test-quality issue rather than a product bug; using `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))` or `findElements().isEmpty()` would be clearer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Failed-login error events are silently discarded in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey: events.clear() is called without asserting the expected LOGIN_ERROR event (Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS, user set)

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`, the test performs an incorrect-password submission (`loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost"))` followed by `Assert.assertEquals("Invalid password.", loginPage.getInputError())`) and then calls `events.clear()` before proceeding to a successful WebAuthn login assertion. This does discard any `LOGIN_ERROR` event that may have been emitted by the failed password attempt, and the test does not assert `EventType.LOGIN_ERROR` / `Errors.INVALID_USER_CREDENTIALS` for that attempt. This is a test coverage/assertion gap rather than a product bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers re-authentication with a non-discoverable key: all new re-auth tests use discoverable/external resident keys despite the conditional-UI re-auth changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple new re-authentication tests (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` in both `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest`, and several `*_reauthentication*` tests in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`), but they all exercise discoverable passkeys or external resident keys (`DefaultVirtualAuthOptions.PASSKEYS` / `DEFAULT_RESIDENT_KEY`). Existing non-discoverable coverage (`passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`) does not include any `prompt=login`/re-authentication flow. Given the PR changes conditional passkeys behavior during re-authentication (e.g., `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`, `UsernameForm` conditional, and `UsernamePasswordForm` passkeys setup when `user != null`), there is a specific missing test case for re-auth with a non-discoverable key scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplication of the 'user already set' auth-note check logic: `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` in AuthenticatorUtils.java:126-129 re-implements the existing `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)` predicate instead of delegating to it, creating two independent implementations that can drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the original inline check `if (isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)) { ... }` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` being replaced by `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)`. The new utility method re-derives the same condition by directly reading the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` and `Boolean.parseBoolean(...)`, rather than delegating to the existing predicate (which is still referenced by name in the removed code and likely still exists in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`). This is a real maintainability/duplication concern (two independent implementations can drift), but not a verifiable functional bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cross-package leak of internal constant: `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` was widened from `protected` to `public` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58 / AuthenticatorUtils.java:35) solely for a static import, promoting an internal stringly-typed protocol into public API surface

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly widens `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `protected static final` to `public static final` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, and `AuthenticatorUtils` then uses it via `import static ...USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH;`. This does increase the public API surface of that class for the sake of cross-package reuse of an internal auth-note key. It’s a valid scope/encapsulation concern grounded in the diff, but it does not by itself demonstrate broken behavior or a correctness/security defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` defined in both UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162 and UsernameForm.java:47 with different signatures and divergent semantics (one requires `user != null`), a drift trap; also the user-null check is a semantic mismatch in a realm-policy 'enabled' check

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm`. In `UsernameForm`, the diff merely changes a condition to call `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (no-arg), but does not show any such method being defined there. Therefore the finding’s core claim that `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is defined in both files with different signatures/semantics is not verifiable from this diff and appears to misread it. The critique about the `user != null` check being a semantic mismatch may be debatable, but the stated “defined in both”/“divergent semantics” is not grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:64-66` unconditionally returns `false` from `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`, making the authenticator-listing branch in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` (lines 100-119) unreachable and making `isUserIdentified` dependent on an overridable hook

adjudication.rationale: The branch in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` guarded by `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` is not unreachable in general: the base implementation added in this diff returns `context.getUser() != null`, so the authenticator-listing code remains reachable for the normal `WebAuthnAuthenticator` path. `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` newly overrides this hook to return `false` intentionally (comment: “Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys”), which only disables that branch for that specific subclass, not globally. Therefore calling it “dead code” / “unreachable” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Three near-verbatim copies of the same re-authentication test across PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:269-318, PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:260-315, and PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest; shared helpers should be extracted for the login/re-auth/event-assert sequences

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds highly similar re-authentication tests in multiple files: `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` is added both to `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest` and `PasskeysUsernameFormTest` with near-identical sequences (configure passkeys, register user, initial passkey login, then `prompt=login` re-auth and identical `events.expectLogin()` assertions). `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` also adds new re-authentication coverage with very similar login + `prompt=login` + event-assert patterns (though for external keys and with extra steps). This is a maintainability/duplication concern in the new tests, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile 'assert element absent' idiom in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest that swallows arbitrary exceptions via `catch (Exception e)`; should use `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` as done in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, and the inconsistency between idioms adds confusion

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest, the new checks for absence of the WebAuthn form use a broad `try { driver.findElement(...) ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }` pattern (e.g., in `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`). This will treat any exception (not just `NoSuchElementException`) as success, making the test fragile and potentially hiding real failures. However, the finding’s claim that PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest uses `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` is not supported by this diff (that file was changed to assert the element is present).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Comment/naming drift in WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:97-101: the `user` local is fetched but the branch condition no longer references it, and the old '2 Factor Scenario' comment no longer matches the code delegated to a hook

adjudication.rationale: In `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`, `user` is still used inside the `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context))` block to build `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean`; the condition was merely refactored behind a hook (`shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`), whose default implementation still checks `context.getUser() != null`. The remaining comment about a “2 Factor Scenario” may be slightly less direct after the refactor, but this is at most a minor comment/style concern, not a concrete review issue grounded in broken behavior or a substantive change problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broker-linked users lose the re-auth fast-path when conditional passkeys are enabled: the hasLinkedBrokers branch in UsernameForm.java:47 is unreachable because the && short-circuits on !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(), forcing all re-authenticating users through the username form with no check for existing passkey credentials

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, which means the “skip username form” fast-path is disabled only when conditional passkeys are enabled. However, the finding’s claim that the `hasLinkedBrokers` branch is “unreachable” is incorrect: it is still executed whenever `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is true. Also, broker-linked users did not have the fast-path before (they already fell into the `hasLinkedBrokers` case and did not `context.success()`), so they are not specifically “losing” a broker-linked re-auth fast-path per this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: User-switch during re-authentication is now possible via the username form: submitted username flows into the normal setUser/user-lookup path without validation that it matches the expected re-auth user, allowing identity switching in step-up flows

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the previous early-exit for re-authentication (`if (context.getUser() != null) { ... context.success(); }`) is now bypassed when conditional passkeys are enabled (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`). This means that during re-auth flows where `context.getUser()` is already set, the username form can now be shown and (by normal UsernameForm behavior) accept a submitted username and proceed through the standard user-lookup/set-user path. The diff does not add any guard that the submitted username must match the pre-set re-auth user; the only re-auth hardening added (`setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError`) applies to username/password error rendering, not to `UsernameForm` submission. This creates a plausible identity-switching vulnerability in step-up re-authentication flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Passkey form data is no longer filled when no user is set due to inverted condition on the error path (UsernamePasswordForm.java:113/137): error re-renders after failed first-attempt silently drop the passkey UI because fillContextForm is never invoked

shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators change in WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:100 makes fillContextForm semantics override-dependent, risking inconsistent behavior with isUserIdentified handling in future subclasses (maintenance hazard)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm` to gate the “user already identified”/authenticator-list branch on a new overridable hook `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` instead of the direct condition `user != null`. This makes `fillContextForm` behavior depend on subclass overrides (as done in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`, which returns `false` even when `context.getUser()!=null`), potentially decoupling the “user identified” state from the branch that sets `isUserIdentified`/populates authenticators. That’s an intentional extensibility point, but it does create a maintenance hazard: future subclasses can inadvertently override the hook in a way that changes `fillContextForm` semantics relative to user-identification assumptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weak assertion pattern in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest: try/catch-fail idiom around driver.findElement can pass for the wrong reason (element present but findElement throwing for timing reasons is swallowed as expected)
